name: Bronchiectasis Exacerbation

possible: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (in chronic, treatment-refractory cases — separate workup)
pathogens.why: Bronchiectasis exacerbations are strongly influenced by individual chronic colonization patterns — Pseudomonas aeruginosa is disproportionately represented compared to typical community-acquired respiratory infections, particularly in patients with more severe or long-standing structural lung disease.

investigations.why: Tracks colonization status over time and directly informs both current and future empiric choices.

investigations.test: Chest X-ray (if new symptoms or to exclude complications)
investigations.why: Excludes pneumonia or other acute complications superimposed on chronic bronchiectatic changes.
Assesses for hypoxia, particularly relevant in patients with significant structural lung disease.

reasonSource: e=>`A known bronchiectasis patient with increased sputum volume/purulence${e.hemoptysis?" and hemoptysis":""} meets criteria for an infective exacerbation. Antibiotic choice should be guided by prior sputum culture history where available, since bronchiectasis patients frequently have chronic colonization with specific organisms (notably Pseudomonas) that recur with each exacerbation.`
